question: A 5-year-old child with a suspected cardiac defect has a chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio 0.62) with increased pulmonary vascular markings and a prominent left atrial shadow. Which cardiac defect does this radiographic pattern MOST strongly suggest?

answers.text: Tetralogy of Fallot — characterised by decreased pulmonary vascular markings and a boot-shaped heart

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: TOF produces the opposite pattern: decreased pulmonary vascularity (oligaemia), a concave pulmonary artery segment, and the classic boot-shaped heart (coeur en sabot) due to right ventricular hypertrophy. Increased pulmonary markings indicate pulmonary plethora from a left-to-right shunt, not TOF.

answers.text: Ventricular septal defect or patent ductus arteriosus — large L-R shunts cause pulmonary plethora and left atrial/ventricular enlargement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Large VSD or PDA produces: (1) increased pulmonary vascular markings (plethora) from L-R shunt overflow; (2) left atrial and left ventricular enlargement (from increased pulmonary venous return); and (3) overall cardiomegaly. CT ratio >0.55 (this child has 0.62) on an adequate inspiratory PA film confirms cardiomegaly. This pattern distinguishes volume-overload L-R shunts from obstructive lesions.

answers.text: Pulmonary stenosis — causes right ventricular hypertrophy and post-stenotic pulmonary artery dilation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pulmonary stenosis causes right ventricular hypertrophy with right-sided cardiomegaly, and may show post-stenotic dilation of the main pulmonary artery. However, pulmonary vascular markings are normal or reduced (not increased), and left atrial enlargement is not a feature of isolated pulmonary stenosis.

answers.text: Tricuspid atresia — presents with left-axis deviation on ECG and decreased pulmonary blood flow

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tricuspid atresia characteristically shows decreased pulmonary blood flow (oligaemia) on CXR and left axis deviation on ECG — the only cyanotic CHD with LAD. The radiographic pattern in this question (plethora + left atrial enlargement) is the opposite of tricuspid atresia.

overallFeedback.feedback: Match the CXR pattern to the haemodynamic mechanism. Pulmonary plethora (increased vascularity) = L-R shunt. Pulmonary oligaemia (decreased vascularity) = R-L shunt or outflow obstruction. Cardiomegaly CT >0.55 on a good inspiratory film is significant.
Well done. Pulmonary plethora + left atrial enlargement + cardiomegaly = large L-R shunt (VSD, PDA, or AVSD). TOF = oligaemia + boot-shaped heart. Tricuspid atresia = oligaemia + LAD on ECG.
